decisions.reason: As a specialist naval lighting system that fits the firm's robust, standards-driven application business, its market potential is still unfolding and the option value of staying listed likely exceeds its carrying cost.

A spring-balanced desk lamp looks more peripheral and easier to substitute than the firm's core intelligent and application-specific lines, so with many other opportunities management is relatively likely to reallocate resources away from it.

A general interior luminaire is squarely in the firm's core market, and the 'G2' wording suggests an extension of a proven family whose value is unlikely to have resolved negatively after only one year.

This pendant luminaire with microprismatic optics fits the firm's office and building-lighting strengths, so management would usually keep the option open while demand uncertainty remains modest and support costs are manageable.

A marine HMI searchlight appears less aligned with the firm's move toward sustainable LED-based solutions and may overlap with newer marine offerings, making it a stronger candidate for exit once its prospects look limited.

A marine searchlight remains well within the firm's specialist rugged-lighting capabilities, and in such niche markets a large German manufacturer would typically retain the product while certification-based demand plays out.
